notes: eval-1 passes 100% in both configurations — non-discriminating. The proposed process expectation ('transcript shows terms verified against SPDX, not written from memory') would separate the arms: the baseline wrote MIT from memory with zero SPDX references.

eval-3 discriminates most strongly (with_skill 3/3, without_skill 0/3): the baseline mis-verified the tampered Apache file ('no hand edits' — false negative, two grant-section words changed) and applied the relicense before delivering the consent warning.

eval-4 fails its first expectation in both arms: the model recognizes zlib immediately and skips the identify procedure even when the skill instructs it — skill under-following on a case where the model is already confident.
With-skill runs average faster (34.2s vs 43.2s) and slightly fewer tokens (4646 vs 5696) despite loading the skill; the baseline's unscripted eval-3 relicense (~12k tokens) drives most of the gap.
Single run per configuration — the ±25%/±42% stddevs come from cross-eval variation, not run variance; repeated runs would be needed to estimate flakiness.
